analysis:
Reviewed scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py, an offline CI test script. Changed ranges are at lines 720-721, 730, 811-814 and 828, all in the base and head versions. The patch edits comments and loosens one regex: the route lane assertion at ~730 no longer requires a trailing ' required' suffix after LANE_SIZE. The visible head text (lines 1-461) and base text (lines 870-1261) contain no changed lines in these ranges, so the changed-line content comes only from the patch excerpt, which is truncated after line 828.

Security relevance: this file is a test-only guard on CI workflow structure. It checks that save-caches is limited to master/dev pushes, that checkouts use persist-credentials: false, that composite cache steps cannot bypass the build, that no backend credentials or secrets appear in the provider job, and that the gate requires every lane. None of these assertions changed in the visible ranges. The loosened route regex only drops the 'required' token from the route line. That token is a runtime routing/fallback behavior in provider-plan.yml and scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py, which are not supplied. So I cannot confirm that removing the 'required' expectation does not reduce enforcement that cloud runner fallback is permitted or forbidden. This is an unverified cross-file contract, not evidence of a regression.

No production code, keys, attestation, prefix-cache (T-041), authorization or WebSocket paths are touched. No threat-model assets (A-001 to A-020) or trust boundaries are affected. No new attack surface is identified.

Remaining question for integration: confirm that provider-plan.yml's route lines and the Darkbloom runner routing intentionally changed so that 'required' is no longer emitted. Also confirm that the truncated patch (after line 828) has no additional security-relevant assertion weakening.
